Hi--

In the spirit of "trying to learn some Lean as a programming language, not just for math" I was writing a tokenizer (see below). First iteration I threaded (fuel : Nat) arguments through everything for use with termination_by.

Then I tried the variant below, which is a bit imperfect. I think using return types of
(String × { q: input.Pos // p ≤ q} ) for the helper functions is not quite the right thing to do (e.g. because it seemed to force me to do the recursion not in tail position...)

Anyhow I thought I'd ask and maybe someone can suggest a better pattern...! Or other suggestions!

Thanks!

(sorry it is a bit long -- I did remove e.g. comment- and numeric- parsers for brevity in posting here).

inductive Token
  | ident (s : String)
  | strLit (s : String)
  | natLit (n : Nat)
  | lbrace | rbrace
  | lbracket | rbracket
  | comma | colon | equals
  | eof
deriving Repr

def isIdentChar (c : Char) : Bool := c.isAlpha || c == '_'

def tokenize (input : String) : List Token :=
  go input.startPos []
where
  go (p : String.Pos input) (acc : List Token) : List Token :=
      if h : p = input.endPos then
        acc.reverse
      else
        let c  := p.get h
        let p' := p.next h
        match c with
        | '{' => go p' (Token.lbrace :: acc)
        | '}' => go p' (Token.rbrace :: acc)
        | '[' => go p' (Token.lbracket :: acc)
        | ']' => go p' (Token.rbracket :: acc)
        | ',' => go p' (Token.comma :: acc)
        | ':' => go p' (Token.colon :: acc)
        | '=' => go p' (Token.equals :: acc)
        | '\x22'  => -- double quote
            let (s, ⟨p'',h''⟩) := scanString p' ""
            have : p < p'' := by
              exact String.Pos.next_le_iff_lt.mp h''
            go p'' (Token.strLit s :: acc)
        | c   =>
          if isIdentChar c then
            let (s,⟨p'',h''⟩) := scanIdent p' (String.singleton c)
            have : p < p'' := by
              exact String.Pos.next_le_iff_lt.mp h''
            go p'' (Token.ident s::acc)
          else if c.isWhitespace then
            go p' acc  -- skip
          else
            go p' acc  -- unknown, skip or error
  termination_by p

  scanString (p : input.Pos) (acc : String) : (String × { q: input.Pos // p ≤ q} ) :=
      if h : p = input.endPos then
        (acc, ⟨p,by simp⟩)  -- unterminated string literal, return what we have
      else
        let c := p.get h
        let p' := p.next h
        have : p ≤ p' := by exact String.Pos.le_next
        if c == '\x22' then
          (acc, ⟨p',by exact String.Pos.le_next⟩)  -- closing quote, done
        else
          let (s,⟨p'',h''⟩) := scanString p' (acc.push c  )
          (s, ⟨ p'', by exact String.Pos.le_trans this h''⟩)
  termination_by p

  scanIdent (p : input.Pos) (acc : String) : (String × { q: input.Pos // p ≤ q } ) :=
      if h : p = input.endPos then
        (acc, ⟨p, by simp⟩)
      else
        let c := p.get h
        let p' := p.next h
        have : p ≤ p' := by exact String.Pos.le_next
        if isIdentChar c then
          let (s,⟨p'',h''⟩) := scanIdent p' (acc.push c)
          (s, ⟨p'', by exact String.Pos.le_trans this h'' ⟩)
        else
          (acc, ⟨p,by exact String.Pos.le_refl p⟩)  -- return p, not p' since we don't consume c
  termination_by p

Consider using String.Slice instead. It has a better API than manipulating String.Pos directly.

For strings that are not unreasonably long, you could iterate over input.toList. For very long strings, you might want to look into Std.Iterator (better termination options) or Std.Stream (simpler interface).
You could use the scanning operations that the standard library ships, namely docs#String.Pos.find and docs#String.Pos.skipWhile

scanString (p : input.Pos) : (String × { q: input.Pos // p ≤ q} ) :=
    let closing := p.find '\x22'
    have hle : p ≤ closing := String.Pos.le_find _ _
    if h : closing ≠ input.endPos then
      ((input.slice _ _ hle).copy, ⟨closing.next h, Std.le_trans hle String.Pos.le_next⟩)
    else
      ((input.slice _ _ hle).copy, ⟨closing, hle⟩) -- Unterminated string literal, use what we have

  scanIdent (p : input.Pos) (acc : String) : (String × { q: input.Pos // p ≤ q } ) :=
    let firstNonIdent := p.skipWhile isIdentChar
    have hle : p ≤ firstNonIdent := String.Pos.skipWhile_le -- NB: this lemma is not in 4.30.0. It is in the current nightly, and before it ships in Lean 4.31.0 I will fix the name so it is correctly called `String.Pos.le_skipWhile`.
    (acc ++ (input.slice _ _ hle).copy, ⟨firstNonIdent, hle⟩)

And, for completeness, here is an implementation of scanString that uses String.Slice to avoid having to carry around proofs:

  scanString (p : input.Pos) (acc : String) : (String × { q: input.Pos // p ≤ q} ) :=
    let (str, pos) := scanString' (input.sliceFrom p).startPos acc
    ⟨str, ⟨String.Pos.ofSliceFrom pos, String.Pos.le_ofSliceFrom⟩⟩

  scanString' {s : String.Slice} (p : s.Pos) (acc : String) : (String × s.Pos) :=
      if h : p = s.endPos then
        (acc, p)  -- unterminated string literal, return what we have
      else
        let c := p.get h
        let p' := p.next h
        if c == '\x22' then
          (acc, p')  -- closing quote, done
        else
          scanString' p' (acc.push c)
  termination_by p

Hey @Julia Markus Himmel thanks for the comments!

I seem to be tending towards use of toList , and actually just doing a foldl over it for the tokenizing. The only thing I seem to lose is that I can't work out how to easily catch -- as a comment starter that way. So I'll using lisp/scheme-style comments ; instead.

But I learned something looking at your use of slice related stuff!

FWIW:

inductive Token
  | ident (s : String)
  | strLit (s : String)
  | natLit (n : Nat)
  | lbrace | rbrace
  | lbracket | rbracket
  | comma | colon | equals
  | eof
  | comment (s : String)
deriving Repr

def Char.isIdentChar (c : Char) := c.isAlpha || c == '_'

inductive CharAccum
  | none
  | string (cs : List Char)
  | digits (cs : List Char)
  | ident (cs : List Char)
  | comment (cs : List Char)

structure Accum where
  chars : CharAccum
  tokens : List Token

def start : Accum := { chars := CharAccum.none, tokens := [] }

def tokenize (input : String) : List Token :=
  let res := input.toList.foldl go start
  res.tokens.reverse
where
  processChar (c:Char) (tokens : List Token) : Accum :=
      match c with
      | '{' => Accum.mk CharAccum.none (Token.lbrace :: tokens)
      | '}' => Accum.mk CharAccum.none (Token.rbrace :: tokens)
      | '[' => Accum.mk CharAccum.none (Token.lbracket :: tokens)
      | ']' => Accum.mk CharAccum.none (Token.rbracket :: tokens)
      | ',' => Accum.mk CharAccum.none (Token.comma :: tokens)
      | ':' => Accum.mk CharAccum.none (Token.colon :: tokens)
      | '=' => Accum.mk CharAccum.none (Token.equals :: tokens)
      | ';' => Accum.mk (CharAccum.comment []) tokens -- start a comment
      | '\x22' =>
        Accum.mk (CharAccum.string []) tokens  -- start a string
      | c =>
        if c.isIdentChar then
          Accum.mk (CharAccum.ident [c]) tokens  -- start an identifier
        else if c.isDigit then
          Accum.mk (CharAccum.digits [c]) tokens  -- start a digit sequence
        else if c.isWhitespace then
          Accum.mk CharAccum.none tokens       -- skip
        else
          Accum.mk CharAccum.none tokens      -- unknown; skip or error

  go (a : Accum) (c:Char) :=
    match a.chars with
    | CharAccum.string cs =>
      match c with
      | '\x22' =>
        let s := String.ofList cs.reverse
        Accum.mk CharAccum.none (Token.strLit s::a.tokens)
      | c =>
        Accum.mk (CharAccum.string (c :: cs)) a.tokens
    | CharAccum.ident cs =>
      if c.isIdentChar then
        Accum.mk (CharAccum.ident (c :: cs)) a.tokens -- continue getting identifier
      else
        let s := String.ofList <| cs.reverse
        processChar c <| Token.ident s :: a.tokens
    | CharAccum.digits cs =>
      if c.isDigit then
        Accum.mk (CharAccum.digits (c :: cs)) a.tokens -- continue getting digits
      else
        let n := (String.ofList cs.reverse).toNat!
        processChar c <| Token.natLit n :: a.tokens
    | CharAccum.comment cs =>
      match c with
      | '\n' =>
        let s := (String.ofList cs.reverse).trimAscii.toString
        Accum.mk CharAccum.none (Token.comment s :: a.tokens)
      | _ =>
        Accum.mk (CharAccum.comment (c:: cs)) a.tokens
    | CharAccum.none =>
      processChar c a.tokens

#eval tokenize "{foo = \"hello\", bar = [11,12], \"baz\"} ; foo bar baz   \nack = \"baz\""

evaluates to 

[Token.lbrace,
 Token.ident "foo",
 Token.equals,
 Token.strLit "hello",
 Token.comma,
 Token.ident "bar",
 Token.equals,
 Token.lbracket,
 Token.natLit 11,
 Token.comma,
 Token.natLit 12,
 Token.rbracket,
 Token.comma,
 Token.strLit "baz",
 Token.rbrace,
 Token.comment "foo bar baz",
 Token.ident "ack",
 Token.equals,
 Token.strLit "baz"]
There is no need to convert the string to a list first, we have docs#String.foldl which is much more efficient.

Aha so literally just snipping the .toList worked!

let res := input.foldl go start
